plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, delicate five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter, often while snow is still on the ground. It is widely cultivated in gardens and for bonsai across East Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom in the cold before other trees, and the fruit is used to make umeboshi pickles and plum wine.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen Australian tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, golden-yellow, fragrant ball-shaped flower clusters. Its sickle-shaped leaves (phyllodes) are blue-green and leathery.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October), with some wattles flowering earlier or later
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It pushes up through frost and snow, often forming large carpets in woodlands and gardens.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a natural antifreeze-like protein that helps them survive freezing temperatures, and they contain galantamine, a compound used in Alzheimer's medication.

plants.name: Plumeria rubra
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical deciduous tree with clusters of highly fragrant, waxy, spiral-shaped flowers. It is common in gardens, temple grounds, and lei-making across warm regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Warm months in the Southern Hemisphere, and in tropical regions it blooms from late winter through summer, including February in places like Australia, Brazil, and Fiji
plants.location: Central America, Mexico, and the Caribbean; widely cultivated in tropical Asia, the Pacific, and Australia
plants.funFact: Frangipani flowers are most fragrant at night to attract sphinx moths, yet they produce no nectar and trick the moths into pollinating them.
